items.applicability: Any consequential choice where the client reports a strong sensed direction, pull, or unease that the available analysis has not yet explained.
counterexamples: A sensed opportunity in a market the client has never operated in, with no pattern of prior exposure: there is no experience base, so the hypothesis carries almost no weight and the framework returns missing evidence instead of a lean.
A gut feeling that appears only after a persuasive pitch: the signal tracks the pitch, not the client's own pattern, and the framework treats it as contamination, not instinct.
items.description: Treat what the client is sensing as a hypothesis informed by their experience, never as proof. Name the sensed claim, identify the experience and pattern underneath it, then test it against the decision's numbers and constraints before it influences a score. This is the Instinct lens operating under the directive's rule that intuition is a hypothesis, and it follows the book's own integration point: experts combine instinct with intellect rather than relying on either alone.
evidence_needed: The client's relevant track record in this kind of decision.
The decision's current numbers (cost, capacity, timing) stated plainly enough to contradict the hypothesis if they do.
failure_modes: Accepting the sensed claim as certainty because it is strongly felt.
Dismissing the sensed claim without recording it, losing the one signal the analysis had not priced in.
Letting the hypothesis silently raise a score without a stated test.
inputs: The client's own statement of what they are sensing.
The experience or pattern the client believes informs it.
The option set and the measurable constraints already on the table.
items.limits: The framework cannot validate a sensed claim. It can only structure the test. When the informing experience cannot be identified, the hypothesis is recorded as ungrounded and given no weight.
items.name: Instinct as Hypothesis
outputs: A named hypothesis with its informing pattern.
The test that would confirm or refute it, and the result when the test is run.
A clear statement when the numbers contradict the instinct, with the conflict left visible for the chair.
preconditions: The client can state what they are sensing in their own words.
At least one checkable fact or figure exists that could contradict the hypothesis.
procedure: Record the sensed claim verbatim in the card's reasoning, labeled as a hypothesis.
Ask what experience or pattern informs it (see questions.json, Instinct Lens).
Run the cheapest decisive test against the numbers already available.
If the test contradicts the hypothesis, say so plainly and score on the evidence; if it supports it, the hypothesis may support, never carry, the recommendation.
questions: What exactly is the client sensing, stated as a claim that could be wrong?
What pattern from their own history informs it?
What is the cheapest fact that would prove it wrong?

items.applicability: Before a major commitment, pivot, hire, or role design, when the client has not yet inventoried the gifts, capacities, and durable fascinations the decision depends on.
counterexamples: An urgent operational fix with a known cause and a short deadline: the inventory adds delay without changing the decision, and the framework stands down.
An inventory that lists only credentials and past job titles: it has decoded nothing about design, and the framework returns it as incomplete.
items.description: Before committing, inventory the client's (or the team's) gifts and instincts and decode the underlying design from durable evidence: what they save, collect, return to, and have enjoyed since early on. The book's Archaeology of Ambition exercise reads a person's saved favorites and collections as evidence of design; its execution system begins with the same internal inventory before any execution phase.
evidence_needed: Concrete artifacts of fascination (saved items, collections, repeated projects), not self-descriptions alone.
A record of which capacities the decision actually requires, so the inventory can be compared against it.
failure_modes: Committing first and inventorying afterward to justify the commitment.
Treating the inventory as a personality exercise with no link to the decision's required capacities.
inputs: The decision under consideration and the capacities it requires.
The client's saved favorites, collections, and recurring projects.
Patterns from earlier work and, where the client offers it, childhood pleasures and long-running interests.
items.limits: The inventory surfaces alignment; it does not create capacity that is not there. A gap between the design found and the capacity required is a finding, not a problem to be argued away.
items.name: Design Inventory Before Commitment
outputs: An inventory of gifts, instincts, and decoded design.
A stated match or gap between the design found and the capacities the decision requires.
Role or option adjustments where the gap is decisive.
preconditions: A concrete decision is on the table whose required capacities can be named.
The client is willing to examine their own patterns as evidence.
procedure: List the capacities the decision requires.
Gather the fascination evidence: favorites, collections, repeated themes.
Decode the design: name the recurring pattern in the client's own terms.
Compare design to required capacities and state the match or gap plainly.
questions: What do you keep saving, collecting, or returning to?
Which of those fascinations has survived every change of job or season?
Does the design this reveals match what this decision will demand of you every week?

items.applicability: Ongoing engagements and repeat councils on the same venture, where drift from the client's own direction accumulates quietly.
counterexamples: A single one-off decision with no continuing engagement: there is no rhythm to check yet, and the framework does not apply.
A client whose circumstances changed materially (new market, new constraints): a changed tempo may be adaptation, not drift, and the check must not score it as failure.
items.description: A periodic self-review that asks whether the client is still in sync with their inner wisdom about their strengths, abilities, talents, and unique contribution, and whether they have started following someone else's tempo. Drawn from the book's Rhythm Check self-review protocol and its execution rule against ignoring your own rhythm.
evidence_needed: The client's earlier statements of direction, so drift can be measured against their own baseline rather than the seat's preference.
failure_modes: Running the check as a ritual with no comparison to earlier commitments.
Using the check to push the client back toward a direction they have deliberately and knowingly revised.
inputs: The client's stated direction from earlier sessions.
The commitments and tempo they are currently actually living.
items.limits: The check measures alignment with the client's own stated direction. It cannot judge whether that direction is wise; other seats and the evidence carry that question.
items.name: Rhythm Check
outputs: An alignment finding: in sync, drifting, or deliberately revised.
The specific commitments that no longer match the stated direction, named for the client to keep, drop, or consciously re-choose.
preconditions: A prior statement of the client's direction exists to compare against.
procedure: Restate the client's own direction from their earlier words.
Compare current commitments and pace against it.
Name each mismatch and ask whether it is drift or a deliberate revision.
Record deliberate revisions as updates to the baseline, not as failures.
questions: Are you in sync with your inner wisdom about your strengths, abilities, talents, and unique contribution?
Whose tempo are you following right now, yours or someone else's?
Which current commitment would your earlier self not recognize?

items.applicability: Any option whose main visible payoff is status, appearance, or the look of momentum: the trophy purchase, the prestige hire, the vanity launch, the credential bought instead of earned.
counterexamples: A visible investment that also buys real practice, such as a certification whose coursework is the training itself: appearance is a byproduct, not the substance, and the screen passes it.
Early spending on credibility in a market where trust is the binding constraint, paired with a real delivery practice: the screen asks for the practice, and if it exists, the option stands.
items.description: Screen each option for the book's Trophy Buyer pattern: acquiring the appearance of winning without the practices of winners. For every option, ask what repeated practice it buys, not what image it projects. The book's quality bar supplies the positive test: genuine engagement with one's calling naturally enhances everything and everyone around it, so an option that enhances nothing but the client's image fails the bar.
evidence_needed: The option's actual operating content: schedule, workload, deliverables, and who does the unglamorous parts.
failure_modes: Rejecting every visible investment as vanity, including ones that buy real practice.
Counting intentions as practices: a plan to practice is not a practice.
inputs: The option set with each option's real content, not its presentation.
items.limits: The screen detects appearance-without-practice. It does not judge whether a genuine practice is well designed; that belongs to the execution-focused seats and the evidence.
items.name: Trophy Buyer Screen
outputs: For each option: the practice it buys, or a plain finding that it buys appearance only.
A quality-bar note: what the option would naturally enhance if the client were genuinely engaged with it.
preconditions: Options are described concretely enough to see their operating content.
procedure: For each option, list the repeated practices it commits the client to.
List what it makes the client look like, separately.
Flag any option where the second list is full and the first is empty.
Require a practice amendment or score the option down with the reason stated.
questions: What will you actually be doing every week if you choose this?
If nobody could see this purchase, would it still be worth its price?
What does this enhance besides how the venture looks?

items.applicability: Every card this seat writes. The pattern is the seat's own operating structure, defined by directive Section 7.3, not a framework from any of the three books.
counterexamples: A narrow factual question inside the seat's domain where only one lens is engaged: forcing all three lenses onto it produces filler, and the pattern expressly forbids that.
items.description: BlackCEO adaptation, not a sourced framework. The seat examines the decision through up to three lenses and integrates the findings into ONE position and ONE vote: the Instinct lens (what is sensed, tested as a hypothesis), the Disruptive Thinking lens (which established assumption needs challenging, with a plausible alternative and a contained test), and the Don't Drop the Mic lens (audience, message, delivery context, comprehension, intended response). Only lenses an option actually engages are used; there is no forced use of all three. Grounding status is asymmetric and is stated on the card: the Instinct lens is grounded in the pack's Instinct evidence; the other two lenses currently operate only at the level of these directive definitions because their books are absent from the source library.
evidence_needed: For the Instinct lens: the hypothesis and its test.
For the Disruptive Thinking lens: the named assumption, the plausible alternative, and the smallest contained test.
For the Don't Drop the Mic lens: the named audience, the message, and the intended response.
failure_modes: Counting three lens findings as three votes or three seats.
Presenting directive-level lens reasoning as if it were drawn from Disruptive Thinking or Don't Drop the Mic the books.
Padding a card with a lens the decision does not engage.
inputs: The decision brief and option set.
The lens findings from the frameworks above.
items.limits: This pattern organizes the seat's reasoning. It adds no source authority: two of its three lenses are ungrounded until their books are ingested, and the card must say so whenever they carry weight.
items.name: Three-Lens Consultation Pattern
outputs: One integrated seat position with lenses_used recorded per finding and a source reference for each grounded finding.
preconditions: The decision engages at least one of the three lenses.
procedure: Run each engaged lens using its framework or, for the ungrounded lenses, its directive definition only.
Record each finding under its lens with its grounding status.
Integrate the findings into one position; where lenses conflict, name the conflict as the seat's stated crux contribution.
Cast one vote.
questions: Which lenses does this decision actually engage?
Where do the lenses agree, and where do they pull against each other?
What is the one position the seat can defend as a whole?

note: Frameworks F1 to F4 are paraphrase-level constructions from the CWE-011 export's Instinct concept evidence (quality unverified, rights reference_only); attribution_kind says so on each item and no verbatim text is used. F5 is an original BlackCEO adaptation of the directive's seat structure and is labeled as such. No framework is attributed to Disruptive Thinking or Don't Drop the Mic: those books are absent from the source library and inventing named frameworks for them is forbidden.
